requirements.title: Hex colours parse as sRGB with a tolerant scanner: an unparseable string yields black rather than failing
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Theme/AppTheme.swift:236-247 `extension Color { init(hex: String) }` - `var text = hex.trimmed` (:239), `if text.hasPrefix("#") { text = String(text.dropFirst()) }`, `Scanner(string: text).scanHexInt64(&value)`, red=(value >> 16) & 0xFF / 255, green=(value >> 8) & 0xFF / 255, blue=value & 0xFF / 255, `self.init(.sRGB, red: red, green: green, blue: blue, opacity: 1)`
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:130-132 `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`
requirements.preconditions: A hex string is turned into a colour.
requirements.action: Color(hex:) is called with a six-digit string, with or without a leading "#", possibly with surrounding whitespace.
requirements.expected_result: The string is trimmed of whitespace and newlines, one leading "#" is dropped, and the remainder is scanned as a hexadecimal integer. Channels are taken as bytes 16..23, 8..15 and 0..7, each divided by 255, in the sRGB space at opacity 1. A string the scanner cannot read leaves the value at 0, producing opaque black: there is no error path and no throw.
failure_cases: Unparseable text: value stays 0 and the colour is #000000 at full opacity. No message, no log.
A string longer than six hex digits: the scanner reads what it can and the high bits above bit 23 are discarded by the masks.
requirements.windows_path: Implement the same tolerant parse, including the black-on-garbage behaviour, so a future palette typo degrades identically. Colours must be treated as sRGB, not as the display's colour space.
requirements.verification_method: unit: parse table including "#CBA6F7", "CBA6F7", " CBA6F7 " and a deliberately invalid string
requirements.b2_change: Re-cited only. AppTheme.swift:239 `var text = hex.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` (B1) -> `var text = hex.trimmed` (B2), and `trimmed` is exactly that trim (B2 Core/Support/Text.swift:132). Range 236-247 and behaviour unchanged.

requirements.preconditions: A downsampled base picture exists.
requirements.action: The picture is softened for a softness value.
requirements.expected_result: The Gaussian radius is softness multiplied by 28 and by the radius scale (1 for the full-size render, the preview-to-base width ratio for a live preview). A radius of 0.01 or less returns the base unchanged, so softness 0 costs nothing. The filter is created by name, and the name is exactly "CIGaussianBlur"; the input image is set under kCIInputImageKey and the radius under kCIInputRadiusKey. The source is clamped to its own extent before blurring and the result cropped back to that extent, taken as the origin plus the base image's pixel width and height, so the picture's outer pixels stay opaque instead of fading to transparent at the window edges. One shared GPU-backed render context is used for every blur, never one per picture.

failure_cases: The blur filter cannot be created: the base is returned unblurred.
The filter produces no output: nothing is returned, and the caller drops the render.
requirements.windows_path: Platform boundary: "CIGaussianBlur" is a Core Image filter identifier with no Windows counterpart, so the Windows build substitutes its own Gaussian blur (Direct2D's Gaussian blur effect or equivalent). The filter's IDENTITY is recorded here so the substitution is a named one rather than a guess, and so the radius semantics can be matched: Core Image's radius parameter is the Gaussian's standard-deviation-derived radius, and a Windows blur whose parameter means something else must be converted rather than passed through. The 28 multiplier, the 0.01 short-circuit, and the clamp-then-crop edge handling are all observable and must match; a blur without edge clamping puts a soft translucent band around the whole window.

requirements.title: The tone generator sums notes of exponentially decaying partials over a raised-cosine attack
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:7-19 Note (frequency, onset, level) and Partial (multiple, level, decay)
DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:22-23 `private static let attack = 0.006` with the comment "A raised-cosine onset: quick enough to feel struck, with no click."

DroppyCode/UI/Sound/ToneSynth.swift:27-40 the loop: `let count = Int(sampleRate * duration)`; per note `let start = Int(note.onset * sampleRate)`; for each index from start, `time = Double(index - start) / sampleRate`, `onset = time < attack ? 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(.pi * time / attack) : 1`, `tone = sum over partials of partial.level * exp(-time / partial.decay) * sin(2 * .pi * note.frequency * partial.multiple * time)`, `samples[index] += note.level * onset * tone`
requirements.preconditions: A note list, a partial list and a duration are given.
requirements.action: The tone is rendered.
requirements.expected_result: The buffer holds floor(44100 times duration) samples. Each note starts at floor(onset times 44100) and runs to the end of the buffer. Within a note, the envelope is 0.5 minus 0.5 times cos(pi times t / 0.006) for the first 6 milliseconds and 1 afterwards. The note's timbre at time t is the sum over its partials of level times exp(-t / decay) times sin(2 pi f multiple t), where f is the note's own frequency. Notes are summed into the same buffer, so overlapping notes add.
failure_cases: None expressed in source.
requirements.windows_path: Pure arithmetic; port it directly in double precision. The partial set is shared by every note of a chime, not per note.
requirements.verification_method: unit: sample-by-sample comparison against the formula for a known note and partial list

requirements.title: List items absorb following lines as continuation text or as nested child blocks, and a list ends when its kind changes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:195-262 parseList: a marker at or above the first item's indent starts a new item, but only when its ordered flag matches the first item's, otherwise the list ends; a line indented past the first item's indent is dropped by the smaller of its indentation and the item's content offset and appended to the child lines, unless the child lines are still empty and the line is neither a marker nor a fence, in which case its trimmed form continues the item's own text; an unindented line continues the item's text only while there are no child lines and it is not a heading, a fence or a quote; anything else ends the list

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:222-234 a blank line is skipped when the next line is indented past the item (recorded as an empty child line) or when the next line is a sibling marker of the same indent and kind; otherwise it ends the list
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:214 each item's children are `parse(childLines[...], depth: depth + 1).blocks`
requirements.preconditions: A list has started.
requirements.action: The parser reads the lines after the first marker.
requirements.expected_result: Sibling items are markers at the same or a smaller indent with the same ordered flag; a marker of the other kind ends the list rather than continuing it. Indented lines become the item's nested blocks, parsed one level deeper, except that indented prose arriving before any nested block simply continues the item's text. Unindented lines continue the item's text only until the item has nested blocks, and never when they are a heading, a fence or a quote. A blank line does not end the list when the next line either is indented content or is a sibling marker; otherwise it does.
failure_cases: None expressed in source; every line either continues, nests or ends the list.
requirements.windows_path: This is the most intricate part of the grammar and the part a CommonMark library will get differently. It must be ported rule by rule and covered by fixtures.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: a list corpus covering loose lists, nested code, mixed markers and blank lines

requirements.title: Line trimming takes a fast path for lines that begin and end with printable ASCII
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownParser.swift:264-270 `trimmed(_ line:)`: when the first and last UTF-8 bytes are both above 0x20 and below 0x7F the line is returned as it is; otherwise it is whitespace-trimmed

requirements.action: The parser trims it.

requirements.title: A finished message renders its blocks as prose runs and standalone blocks; a streaming one renders every block separately
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:25-45 `segments(_:)`: headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes accumulate into a prose run; code, tables and rules close the run and stand alone

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:63-102 the body: when not streaming, the segments are rendered as ProseRunView for a run and MarkdownBlockView for a standalone block; while streaming, every block is a MarkdownBlockView carrying `settled: index < stable` and the streaming environment set only on the last block; both arms use a VStack of alignment leading and spacing 12 and set the veiled environment for the whole message
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:9-23 the view is Equatable on text and the streaming flag, so finished replies are skipped entirely while a new reply streams
requirements.preconditions: A message is being rendered.
requirements.action: Its blocks are laid out.
requirements.expected_result: Blocks are stacked leading-aligned with 12 points between them. A finished message groups consecutive headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes into one prose run rendered as a single text object, breaking the run at each code block, table or rule, which render as their own views. A streaming message renders every block on its own, marks blocks below the stable count as settled, and marks only the last block as streaming. The whole message is marked veiled while it streams, so every block dissolves its arriving text, not only the last.
failure_cases: None expressed in source.
requirements.windows_path: The two paths produce visibly different typography (the run path is one native text object, the block path is a stack of views), and a message swaps from one to the other when its stream ends. requirements.verification_method: interaction test: a reply's layout when streaming and after it finishes; unit: the segment grouping

requirements.title: Blocks compare by content, except that two blocks both marked settled compare equal without looking at their content
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:278-298 MarkdownBlockView is Equatable: `nonisolated static func == (lhs: MarkdownBlockView, rhs: MarkdownBlockView) -> Bool { if lhs.settled, rhs.settled { return true }; return lhs.block == rhs.block }` (:295-298), with the comment (:280-283) that comparing every byte of every earlier block of the reply on every flush is work the flush does not need
requirements.preconditions: A streaming reply flushes.
requirements.action: The view tree is diffed.

requirements.windows_path: An equality short-circuit keyed on the parser's stability claim. A port that diffs by value everywhere is behaviourally identical but slower on long replies.
requirements.verification_method: unit: two settled views compare equal even with different content, which is the documented contract

requirements.preconditions: A paragraph names one or more heads.
requirements.action: The paragraph is built.
requirements.expected_result: This row covers the native NSAttributedString path only; the SwiftUI Text path is PR-THEME-177 and the no-target fallback common to both is PR-THEME-178. Each mention becomes a tinted dragon glyph at 1.25 times the base point size, rounded, baseline-offset by the base font's descender plus one, then a space in the base font and the surrounding text colour, then the head's name in the bold face in the head's own colour. requirements.title: A spinner cell's opacity curve is full at 0, smoothsteps to 0.1 by 45 percent, holds to 92 percent, then rises linearly back to full

DroppyCode/UI/Common/WorkingIndicators.swift:34-44 `static func opacity(phase: Double) -> Double { var p = phase.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1); if p < 0 { p += 1 }; if p < 0.45 { let t = p / 0.45; return 1 - (1 - dim) * (t * t * (3 - 2 * t)) }; if p < 0.92 { return dim }; let t = (p - 0.92) / 0.08; return dim + (1 - dim) * t }`

requirements.action: The curve is evaluated for that phase.
requirements.expected_result: The phase is first wrapped into [0, 1) by taking the remainder modulo 1 and adding 1 when the result is negative, so a negative phase (a cell lagging the wave) is valid input. Below 0.45 the value is 1 minus (1 - 0.1) times the smoothstep t*t*(3 - 2*t) with t = p / 0.45, so it falls from 1 to 0.1 with zero slope at both ends. From 0.45 up to 0.92 the value is exactly 0.1. From 0.92 to 1 the value rises linearly from 0.1 back to 1 with t = (p - 0.92) / 0.08. The fall takes 45 percent of the period, the hold 47 percent and the rise 8 percent: the curve has one soft edge and one sharp one and is not symmetric.

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:494 the comment `// A link in a Text keeps the colour the attribute sets and opens through the environment.`

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:495-501 `if let target = hydraMentionTargets[persona.name] { var name = AttributedString(persona.name); name.link = target.url; name.foregroundColor = persona.color; name.inlinePresentationIntent = .stronglyEmphasized; return Text("\(glyph) \(Text(name))") }`
DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:502-503 `let name = Text(verbatim: persona.name).fontWeight(.bold).foregroundColor(persona.color); return Text("\(glyph) \(name)")`

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:385-386 `/// Lifts the 16pt glyph off the baseline onto the surrounding text's x-height.` with `private static func mentionGlyphOffset(size: CGFloat) -> CGFloat { -(size * 0.2) }`

DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:388-393 `/// The head's dragon as a template image small enough to sit in a Text run. Redrawn once per (asset, size), then kept; tinted like the name.` with the cache keyed `persona.asset + "@\(size)"`
requirements.preconditions: A paragraph naming a head is being rendered through the SwiftUI text path (not the native attributed path, which is PR-THEME-143).
requirements.action: A mention is turned into text.
requirements.expected_result: The glyph is the head's dragon at a fixed 16 points, coloured with the persona's colour and given a baseline offset of -3.2 points (`-(size * 0.2)` with size 16). The source comment at MarkdownView.swift:385 says the offset "Lifts the 16pt glyph off the baseline onto the surrounding text's x-height", but the value is negative, and in SwiftUI a positive baseline offset raises text, so the code lowers the glyph where the comment says it lifts it: comment and code disagree. The port reproduces the code's value, -3.2, not the comment. The glyph is drawn from a cache keyed by the asset name and the size. When the chat has a target for that head, the name is an attributed string carrying THREE attributes: a real link whose value is the target's URL, the persona's own foreground colour, and the strongly-emphasized inline presentation intent. The link attribute is deliberate here, contrary to the native path: the source's own comment records that a link inside a Text keeps whatever colour the attribute sets and opens through the environment, so the persona colour survives and the accent recolouring that afflicts a native text view does not apply. The result is the glyph, a space, and the attributed name.
requirements.persistence: A process-lifetime glyph cache keyed by asset and size.
requirements.windows_path: This path and the native path differ in kind, not only in glyph size: this one produces a real hyperlink attribute and the native one a custom non-link attribute (PR-THEME-143). Both must be reproduced as written. If the Windows text stack recolours links the way a native macOS text view does, the explicit foreground colour must be applied after the link so the persona colour still wins.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting the three attributes on the name run, plus a capture comparison of the glyph size and baseline offset against the native path's
requirements.b2_change: Glyph size `let size = 16 * zoom` (B1 MarkdownView.swift:491) -> `let size: CGFloat = 16` (B2 :490); re-cited B1 :490-494 -> B2 :489-493. The three name attributes and the plain fallback are unchanged.

String(match.output.2) : "\(match.output.1) (\(match.output.2))" }`; `text = text.replacing(#/<((?:https?|mailto):[^<>\s]+)>/#) { $0.output.1 }`; `return text`

git diff dd2b86ef..1fbf81e -- DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/SelectableMessageText.swift: B1 :55-59 ran the same three patterns through `NSRegularExpression` via a private `replace` helper (B1 :63-79) that matched over `NSRange(text.startIndex..., in: text)`, that is UTF-16
requirements.preconditions: Copy message is chosen on a reply whose headings, paragraphs or list items contain image markup, links or angle-bracket autolinks.
requirements.action: Each such text is passed through inline().
requirements.expected_result: Three passes run in this order over the whole text. First every `![alt](target)` whose target has no whitespace becomes its alt text, which may be empty. Then every `[title](target)`, with a non-empty title free of square brackets, a target without whitespace, and optionally whitespace and a double-quoted title attribute before the closing parenthesis, becomes the target alone when title and target are equal, otherwise `title (target)`. Then every `<http:...>`, `<https:...>` or `<mailto:...>` with no whitespace or angle bracket inside becomes the bare address. The passes use Swift's Regex, whose default matching unit is the Character (an extended grapheme cluster): a combining mark attached to a bracket, parenthesis or angle bracket makes one character with it, so that bracket no longer matches the pattern's literal. Ordinary text gives the same output as B1.
failure_cases: No failure path: a text with no match is returned unchanged.
requirements.windows_path: Port the three patterns and their order verbatim, and match over user-perceived characters (grapheme clusters), not UTF-16 code units, to reproduce B2 at combining marks. The grapheme-level difference is derived from reading the code and Swift's documented Regex semantics, not from running it on a Mac.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: recorded plain-text output for images, titled links, links whose title equals the URL, links with a quoted title attribute, and the three autolink schemes; unit: the text made of `[`, U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT and `t](https://a.b)` is left unrewritten
requirements.b2_change: New at B2: inline() moved from NSRegularExpression (B1 SelectableMessageText.swift:54-79) to Swift Regex `String.replacing` (B2 :54-63) with the same patterns and transforms; only the matching unit differs.

ui.notes: Exactly two sections exist at this commit. These are the only colours in the theme area declared as floating-point components rather than hex, and they take the framework's default colour space, which is sRGB.

ui.screen: Chat, working line; also sidebar rows, helper stubs, team panels and MCP rows
ui.geometry: 3 columns by 3 rows; cell size 3.5 points by default; inter-cell gap 0.8 times the cell size on both axes; content size 3*3.5 + 2*2.8 = 16.1 points square at the default size; centred in the offered frame with the origin rounded to whole points; row 0 at the top
ui.typography: Not text
ui.colors: Three row tints from the theme accent in sRGB: accent blended 0.38 toward white (top row), the accent itself (middle row), accent blended 0.22 toward black (bottom row)
states: running: each cell pulses once per 0.75 s on a 41-sample linear keyframe, lagged by hypot(column-1, 2-row)/2.5 so the wave travels upward from the bottom-centre cell
reduce motion: no animation; each cell frozen at the curve evaluated at minus its lag
theme or appearance change: cells retint instantly, with no crossfade
interactions: none; hit tests pass straight through to the row beneath

ui.colors: Stage fill: the label colour at 6 percent, at 10 percent when hovered or chosen. Symbol: the theme accent when chosen, Chrome.secondaryText (the label colour at 70 percent) otherwise. ED-062: Chrome.secondaryText is Chrome.primaryText at opacity 0.7, as B2 defines it (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:79); ED-051's secondaryLabelColor literal is superseded for this token.

chosen: fill 0.10, accent symbol, accent ring, primary caption, selected accessibility trait
no pressed or disabled styling of its own
interactions: click selects the option
accessibility label is the title verbatim

SF Symbols are drawn as their Lucide counterparts from the published symbol-by-symbol table (owner ruling OD-0010). OD-0014: the window stays clear by default, as upstream, so until the user sets a wallpaper the desktop shows through as Acrylic plus the app-drawn scrim (OD-0005).

deviation.upstream: The strip is drawn with `.chromeGlassCapsule()` (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/ChromeSegmentedPicker.swift:39), which renders `content.glassEffect(.regular.tint(Chrome.glassTint.opacity(0.3)).interactive(), in: shape)` (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:180), macOS Liquid Glass
deviation.port: Where the window behind the control shows the desktop, an Acrylic-class Windows system material, without lensing, refraction or chromatic fringing; where the app draws its own backdrop (the wallpaper or the solid base), a shader reproduces the source-defined material: shape, corner radius, tint colour and opacity, .interactive() and container spacing
